explanation: Ultraviolet B rays turn a cholesterol-based substance in the skin into vitamin D. The body needs it to absorb calcium from food and build strong bones.

claims.text: Human skin makes vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet B light from the Sun.
The skin does not make vitamin C, vitamin A or vitamin B12 from sunlight.
Ultraviolet B light turns 7-dehydrocholesterol, a cholesterol-related compound in the skin, into a form of vitamin D.
Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium from food, which bones need.
